questions.q: What is the toe of a weld?
o: The deepest point of the joint
The junction between the weld face and base metal
questions.ref: AWS A3.0, Standard Welding Terms and Definitions; AWS A2.4, Standard Symbols for Welding, Brazing, and Nondestructive Examination
questions.n: AWS terminology defines the weld toe as the junction of the weld face and the base metal.

questions.q: Which framing system provides lateral rigidity through rigid beam-column connections that transfer bending moments?
questions.ref: AISC Steel Construction Manual and AISC structural steel terminology
questions.n: Moment-resisting frames rely on rigid beam-column joints to resist lateral loads through bending action.

questions.q: What type of metal deck is used primarily as permanent formwork for reinforced concrete without relying on composite slab action?
questions.ref: Steel Deck Institute, Composite Steel Floor Deck and deck terminology
questions.n: Form deck serves as permanent stay-in-place formwork for concrete but is not designed to act compositely with the slab after curing.

questions.q: What type of steel deck is designed to act compositely with a concrete slab?
questions.ref: Steel Deck Institute, Composite Steel Floor Deck and deck terminology
questions.n: Composite steel floor deck is profiled to mechanically interlock with concrete and participate in composite slab action.

questions.q: What is a gusset plate?
o: A plate used to connect multiple structural members at a joint
questions.ref: AISC Steel Construction Manual and AISC structural steel terminology
questions.n: Gusset plates are connection plates used at truss, bracing, and frame joints to join multiple members.

questions.q: Why are moment connections important in a moment-resisting frame?
o: They transfer bending moments between beams and columns
questions.ref: AISC Steel Construction Manual and AISC structural steel terminology
questions.n: Moment connections provide rotational restraint and transfer bending moments between connected members.

questions.q: Which semi-finished steel product is typically rectangular and relatively wide, serving as feedstock for plate and sheet rolling?
questions.ref: ASM International, Metals Handbook / standard metal product terminology
questions.n: A slab is a broad, rectangular semi-finished steel product used as feedstock for flat-rolled products.

questions.q: Who typically prepares structural-steel shop and erection drawings from the engineer's design documents?
questions.ref: AISC Steel Construction Manual and AISC structural steel terminology
questions.n: Steel detailers prepare shop and erection drawings that translate design information into fabrication and erection instructions.

questions.q: Which metal is not generally classified as a noble metal?
questions.ref: ASM International, Metals Handbook / standard metal product terminology
questions.n: Gold, platinum, and palladium are commonly classed among noble metals; titanium is a reactive/passivating metal rather than a noble metal.

questions.q: What is the root of a weld?
o: The outermost edge of the weld face
The portion of the joint where the members are closest to each other and where the weld begins at the deepest point
questions.ref: AWS A3.0, Standard Welding Terms and Definitions; AWS A2.4, Standard Symbols for Welding, Brazing, and Nondestructive Examination
questions.n: AWS defines the weld root as the points or line where the back of the weld intersects the base-metal surfaces or where the members are closest, depending on joint geometry.

questions.q: What process creates a hard, protective oxide layer on aluminum by electrolytic treatment?
questions.ref: Aluminum Association, Aluminum Design Manual / anodizing terminology
questions.n: Anodizing is an electrochemical process that thickens and stabilizes the natural aluminum oxide layer.

questions.q: What does the abbreviation HSS mean in structural steel construction?
questions.ref: ASTM A500/A500M - Cold-Formed Welded and Seamless Carbon Steel Structural Tubing
questions.n: AISC and ASTM use HSS for hollow structural sections such as square, rectangular, and round structural tubing.

questions.q: A field welder uses a flux-coated consumable rod held manually while an electric arc melts the rod and base metal. Which process is this?
questions.ref: AWS D1.1/D1.1M, Structural Welding Code — Steel
questions.n: A manually held flux-coated consumable electrode is characteristic of Shielded Metal Arc Welding.

questions.q: What is a steel plate with a raised waffle or diamond pattern used for vehicle and workshop floors called?
questions.ref: Cyril M. Harris, Dictionary of Architecture and Construction - metalwork, fasteners, and construction terminology
questions.n: Checkered plate has a raised tread pattern that improves slip resistance on floors, stairs, and platforms.

questions.q: Which shapes are commonly produced as HSS?
questions.ref: ASTM A500/A500M - Cold-Formed Welded and Seamless Carbon Steel Structural Tubing
questions.n: ASTM A500 covers cold-formed welded and seamless structural tubing in round, square, rectangular, and special shapes.

questions.q: Aside from corrosion resistance, which property is a major reason stainless steel is selected for exposed architectural applications?
questions.ref: ASM International, Metals Handbook / standard metal product terminology
questions.n: Stainless steel is widely used architecturally for its durable corrosion resistance and distinctive exposed finish.

questions.q: What general term is used for standard steel shapes such as flats, rounds, squares, and angles sold for fabrication?
questions.ref: ASM International, Metals Handbook / standard metal product terminology
questions.n: Merchant bars are standard hot-rolled sections such as flats, rounds, squares, and certain small shapes supplied for general fabrication.

questions.q: Which welding process is commonly called stick welding?
questions.ref: AWS D1.1/D1.1M, Structural Welding Code — Steel
questions.n: SMAW uses a flux-coated consumable electrode and is widely known as stick welding.

questions.q: What is the principal purpose of anodizing architectural aluminum?
o: To remove the oxide layer permanently
To improve surface durability and corrosion resistance while providing a controlled finish
questions.ref: Aluminum Association, Aluminum Design Manual / anodizing terminology
questions.n: Architectural anodizing increases the protective oxide thickness and provides durable decorative finishes.

questions.q: Which process uses a continuously fed wire electrode with externally supplied shielding gas?
questions.ref: AWS A3.0, Standard Welding Terms and Definitions; AWS A2.4, Standard Symbols for Welding, Brazing, and Nondestructive Examination
questions.n: GMAW uses a continuously fed consumable wire electrode and shielding gas.

questions.q: What term applies to extremely thin metal product, typically thinner than ordinary sheet?
questions.ref: ASM International, Metals Handbook / standard metal product terminology
questions.n: Foil is the term used for metal rolled to very small thicknesses, thinner than conventional sheet.

questions.q: What is the headed steel element welded to a beam flange to transfer shear between the beam and concrete slab?
questions.ref: AISC composite construction guidance - headed steel stud anchors
questions.n: Headed stud anchors are welded to steel beams to transfer longitudinal shear and develop composite action with the concrete slab.

questions.q: Where are gusset plates commonly found?
questions.ref: AISC Steel Construction Manual and AISC structural steel terminology
questions.n: Gusset plates are common where several tension/compression members meet in trusses and bracing systems.

questions.q: Which tool tightens or loosens nuts and bolts using rapid repeated torque impulses?
questions.ref: Cyril M. Harris, Dictionary of Architecture and Construction - metalwork, fasteners, and construction terminology
questions.n: An impact wrench applies repeated high-torque impacts to rotate threaded fasteners.

questions.q: What is the principal purpose of a shop drawing in structural steelwork?
o: To serve only as a marketing image
To replace the structural design calculations entirely
To communicate fabrication details, dimensions, connections, and piece information
questions.ref: AISC Steel Construction Manual and AISC structural steel terminology
questions.n: Shop drawings provide the information needed to fabricate individual steel pieces and assemblies.

questions.q: What is the purpose of backing at the root side of a groove weld?
o: To serve only as a decorative plate
To support molten weld metal and help obtain sound root fusion
questions.ref: AWS A3.0, Standard Welding Terms and Definitions; AWS A2.4, Standard Symbols for Welding, Brazing, and Nondestructive Examination
questions.n: AWS terminology describes backing as material placed at the root of a weld joint to support molten weld metal.

questions.q: A concrete floor slab must act together with the supporting steel beam. Which connector should be welded to the top flange?
questions.ref: AISC composite construction guidance - headed steel stud anchors
questions.n: Headed studs provide the shear transfer needed for composite beam action.

questions.q: A multistory steel building has no diagonal bracing and relies on rigid beam-column joints to resist wind drift. What lateral system is being used?
questions.ref: AISC Steel Construction Manual and AISC structural steel terminology
questions.n: If lateral resistance is provided by rigid beam-column joints instead of diagonal bracing, the system is a moment-resisting frame.

questions.q: What is the primary structural function of headed shear studs in a composite floor system?
o: To make the concrete slab and steel beam act compositely by transferring interface shear
questions.ref: AISC composite construction guidance - headed steel stud anchors
questions.n: Shear studs transfer horizontal shear at the steel-concrete interface so the two materials act together as a composite member.

questions.q: What is a set screw?
o: A screw, usually headless, used to secure one component relative to another
questions.ref: Cyril M. Harris, Dictionary of Architecture and Construction - metalwork, fasteners, and construction terminology
questions.n: Set screws are typically headless or nearly headless threaded fasteners tightened against a shaft or component to prevent relative movement.

questions.q: Which of the following is not a semi-finished steel product?
questions.ref: ASM International, Metals Handbook / standard metal product terminology
questions.n: Billets, blooms, and slabs are semi-finished steel forms; clinker is associated with cement manufacture, not steelmaking.
